title: isActive() classifies each scan status as active or terminal correctly
description: CloudPostureScan.isActive() drives whether the reconciler, cancellation, and delete-guard logic treat a scan as in-flight. pending/validating/queued/initializing/running/processing/processing_results/cancelling must return true; completed/completed_with_warnings/failed/cancelled/timed_out/abandoned must return false.
steps: Construct a CloudPostureScan document with status='running' (and each other status in the active set) and call isActive()
Construct a CloudPostureScan document with status='completed' (and each other status in the terminal set) and call isActive()
expectedResult: isActive() returns true for all 8 active-set statuses and false for all 6 terminal-set statuses, with no status missing from either set.

title: calculateProgress() prefers totalSteps/completedSteps over totalChecks/checksCompleted when both are present
expectedResult: progress.percentage is set to 40 (based on totalSteps/completedSteps), not 50 (which the totalChecks/checksCompleted branch would have produced).

title: nextRun() advances the occurrence date deterministically per frequency
description: Scheduler correctness for recurring scans depends on nextRun() producing the exact next UTC timestamp for hourly/daily/weekly/monthly cadences.
steps: Call nextRun(new Date('2026-07-22T00:00:00Z'), 'daily' or an unrecognized frequency string)
expectedResult: hourly returns 2026-07-22T01:00:00.000Z; weekly returns 2026-07-29T00:00:00.000Z; monthly rolls the UTC month forward by 1; daily/unrecognized falls back to +1 UTC day (the scheduler's default branch).

title: toSafeJSON() strips raw provider secrets and exposes only has*/isConfigured booleans
description: CloudPostureConfig.toSafeJSON() is the only sanitizer between the Mongo document and the API response. If it regresses, raw AWS/GCP/Azure secrets could be serialized to the client.
steps: Build a CloudPostureConfig document where providers.aws.credentialConfigured=true and providers.aws.credentials contains legacy fields (accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, region, accountId)
expectedResult: The returned object never contains accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken, serviceAccountKey, clientId, clientSecret, tenantId, or vaultPath for any provider; instead it contains hasAccessKeyId/hasSecretAccessKey/isConfigured (aws), hasServiceAccountKey/isConfigured (gcp), and hasClientId/hasClientSecret/hasTenantId/hasSubscriptionId/isConfigured (azure), all derived from credentialConfigured.

title: findingCheckId() falls back through the identity chain in priority order
description: findingCheckId() is the join key used by finding-compliance.service and the executive-dashboard compliance sync to match a Finding back to scanner_check_master. It must prefer finding.checkId, then prowlerRaw.metadata.event_code, then prowlerRaw.check_id/CheckID, then the evidence.rawData mirrors, then ruleId.
steps: Call findingCheckId({ checkId: 'a', prowlerRaw: { metadata: { event_code: 'b' } }, ruleId: 'c' })
Call findingCheckId({ prowlerRaw: { metadata: { event_code: 'b' } }, ruleId: 'c' })
expectedResult: Results are 'a', 'b', 'c', '' respectively — the highest-priority non-empty source always wins.

title: AWS accountId is rejected unless it is exactly 12 numeric digits
description: validateCredentials('aws', creds) in config.controller.js is the last server-side gate before an AWS credential bundle is written to Vault.
steps: Call validateCredentials('aws', { accessKeyId: 'AKIA...', secretAccessKey: 'x', region: 'us-east-1', accountId: '123456789012' })
expectedResult: The 12-digit numeric accountId passes; a 5-digit value and an alphanumeric value both fail with 'AWS accountId must be exactly 12 numeric digits'.

title: GCP serviceAccountKey must be valid JSON or credential validation fails fast
expectedResult: A well-formed JSON key string passes; a malformed string fails with 'GCP serviceAccountKey must be valid JSON', never reaching Vault or the Prowler validation call.

title: getScanProgressCacheKey() namespaces the Redis key by environment
description: Guards against progress bleed between development/staging/production if ENVIRONMENT is misconfigured — the worker and API must compute the identical key.
expectedResult: Returns 'prowler-development:scan:scan-external-1', matching exactly what the Python worker writes to Redis.
